text.tspan: How the components talk to each other
REST through the Gateway and the Message Broker, gRPC and topic events between services, and the one direct path: the game WebSocket
A · A PLAYER'S REST REQUEST, END TO END
2 read the session gw:session:<jti> in Redis
3 look the route up in config/routes.json
4 cacheable GET? look it up in Redis
6 queue it on that service's FIFO queue
7 pick an instance: Service Discovery's list,
9 nothing works → dead letter, and an
error answer goes back to the Gateway
11 business logic on its own DB
REST), or publish a topic event
the answer returns the same way; the Gateway stores a cacheable 200 in Redis (X-Cache: MISS) and every hop logs the same X-Request-Id
B · WHO CALLS WHOM (ALWAYS THROUGH THE BROKER)
• Player and Resource Service call nobody; Base Service is called by nobody.
• A caller sends to the broker: REST on :8090 with X-Broker-Service, or gRPC on :9090.
• The broker delivers gRPC to the instance's grpc_url (:50051) that Service Discovery lists.
• Contracts: proto/<service>/v1/*.proto. REST stays as the fallback when BROKER_GRPC_URL is empty.
C · TOPIC EVENTS (PUBLISH / SUBSCRIBE THROUGH THE BROKER)
Delivered as POST /internal/events/<topic> or gRPC events.v1.Events/Deliver · durable in SQLite ·
retried, then dead-lettered · each service registers the topics it wants with Service Discovery
D · LIVE GAME OVER WEBSOCKET (NEGOTIATED BY THE GATEWAY, THEN DIRECT)
2 sign a 30 s ticket for this player + lobby (WS_TICKET_SECRET)
5 verify the ticket, join lobby:{id}; push progress, attacks, day/night
